limitations: These contracts record source inspection only; they do not prove ASEN runtime behavior or retrieval parity.
Whitespace and quote-only SQLite outcomes are unproved even though the generated empty expressions are source-inspected.
The configured search cap is not universally 20, and no runtime override or default-window behavior is proved here.
ID retrieval and all-project search are not authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, or implicit project isolation.
Read-side persistence is unproved; inspected SQL reads and in-memory activity or nudges do not establish zero persistent writes.
Retrieval does not redact legacy or imported data merely because normal writers replace private tags.
Live envelopes, actual SQLite matching, configuration overrides, privacy, and provenance remain pending runtime obligations.

cases.summary: Get-by-ID is globally unscoped while ordinary search applies its separately resolved normalized project filter.
cases.contract: The store get selects a complete undeleted row by ID without project filtering. HTTP get follows that behavior. MCP resolves project only after retrieval for its response envelope. Normal MCP search resolves and normalizes a project; all_projects bypasses resolution, while personal scope without an explicit override clears the filter.
cases.negativeControls: No project authorization, tenant boundary, or implicit global isolation is claimed. Soft-deleted rows remain excluded.

cases.summary: Match mode is validated before query branching, with distinct all-term and any-term quoting helpers.
cases.contract: All/default uses whitespace fields, trims edge quotes, doubles every interior quote, quotes every resulting field, and does not drop quote-only fields. Any uses Unicode fields, drops edge-quote-only empties, preserves order and duplicates, doubles interior quotes while preserving already doubled pairs, and joins phrases with OR.
cases.negativeControls: The empty expression generated from whitespace or an any-mode quote-only query is pinned, but its actual SQLite error or zero-row outcome is not claimed.

cases.summary: Any term shorter than three Unicode runes switches the whole observation query to escaped literal LIKE matching.
cases.contract: The fallback searches six fields using literal contains patterns, escapes backslash then percent and underscore, combines fields with OR, combines terms with AND for all/default or OR for any, returns rank zero, and orders updated time then ID descending.
cases.negativeControls: The threshold counts Unicode runes rather than UTF-8 bytes. LIKE is not regexp, glob, raw SQL wildcard matching, or ordinary trigram FTS.

cases.summary: Search defaults to ten and caps at configured MaxSearchResults while topic hits and FTS ranking retain distinct ordering rules.
cases.contract: A nonpositive request limit becomes ten and is capped by configuration, whose default is twenty. Slash-containing exact topic hits rank at negative one thousand, order newest updated first, and are deduplicated before normal results. FTS exposes raw BM25 but orders by a multiplicative composite and stable sync-or-ID then ID keys.
cases.negativeControls: Twenty is a default configuration value, not a universal cap. Default runtime configuration and overrides are not proved by this fixture.

cases.summary: Preview search selects three hundred SQLite characters while full search and ID retrieval retain complete content.
cases.contract: SQLite substr and length define a 300-codepoint preview and truncation flag. MCP search uses previews, compact mode adds preview and truncated structured metadata, and full content requires the separate ID retrieval path.
cases.negativeControls: The bound is not UTF-8 bytes, full bodies are not clamped by search preview behavior, and automatic full-content follow-up is not proved.

cases.summary: Deleted filtering, optional metadata, project profiles, and relation-load error handling remain distinct read contracts.
cases.contract: Get, topic-direct, FTS, and LIKE paths exclude soft-deleted observations. MCP omits absent project, topic, and review metadata. Relation batch-load failures are swallowed unless cancellation or deadline expiry is observed.
cases.negativeControls: No zero-persistent-write claim is made. Read responses do not retroactively redact legacy data, and project-selection profiles do not establish authorization.
